title: Non-blocking findings from PR #417's review (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups)
description: pr-reviewer accepted PR #417 (the bare-package-specifier false-positive fix for the e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import rule) after independently re-verifying every claim in the PR description. A backgrounded code-review pass launched during that same review returned its result only after the accept verdict was already posted and the task moved to docs/tasks/done/; its two findings were independently re-verified afterward and judged non-blocking (so the accept verdict stands), but are tracked here per CLAUDE.md's rule that every non-blocking finding gets a tracked follow-up task, not just a PR/task-review comment.

checklist.step: The new `isBlockedSrcSource` early-return (`if (!rawSource.startsWith('.')) return false`, frontend/eslint.config.js) un-flags a root-absolute specifier like `/src/pages/Something`, which main's pre-PR#417 version of the rule did flag (verified empirically: checked out main's eslint.config.js and confirmed it flags `/src/utils/format`, while PR #417's version doesn't). Vite's own dev-server resolver does resolve a root-absolute specifier against the project root (confirmed via a throwaway `server.pluginContainer.resolveId('/src/utils/format')` probe resolving to the real file), so this isn't a purely theoretical specifier shape for this toolchain -- but `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` independently rejects the same specifier with `TS2307: Cannot find module`, and empirically running an e2e spec containing this import through the actual `yarn playwright test` runner fails hard with `Error: Cannot find module '/src/pages/Something' imported from ...` before any test executes (Playwright's Node-based test runner resolves a leading-`/` specifier as an absolute filesystem path, not as Vite-root-relative). So there's no working, silent bypass of the e2e black-box boundary today -- only a narrower error-reporting mechanism (tsc/runtime crash instead of eslint) for an already-unreachable-in-practice specifier shape. Worth either tightening the gate to also reject a leading `/`/`~` (not just requiring a leading `.`), or at minimum disclosing it in docs/architecture/Testing.md as a known residual gap the way the dynamic-template-literal case already is.

The custom `e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import` rule (and its `isBlockedSrcSource`/`BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT` helpers, frontend/eslint.config.js) has no persisted automated test of its own -- every fix across this rule's whole history (allowlist->regex, path-traversal bypass, bare-utils-barrel false positive, PR #417's bare-package-specifier false positive) has been verified only via a manual probe file written, run through `yarn eslint`, and deleted before commit, per each PR's own description. Each round has independently found a different edge case in the same regex-based logic (PR #417's own fix is itself fixing a hole introduced by an earlier round) -- a persisted test (e.g. a vitest-driven `RuleTester` suite, or a small harness that imports `isBlockedSrcSource` directly and asserts the full edge-case matrix already enumerated across these PR descriptions) would have a better chance of catching the next regression than a one-off manual probe that never survives to the next round. Worth adding such a test.

decisions.decision: Fixed the root-absolute false negative by changing isBlockedSrcSource's early-return guard from `if (!rawSource.startsWith('.')) return false` to `if (!rawSource.startsWith('.') && !rawSource.startsWith('/')) return false` -- i.e. admitting a root-absolute specifier (leading `/`) into the normalize-then-regex check on the same footing as a relative one, while still exempting a bare (`my-package/src/foo`) or @scoped (`@scope/pkg/src/foo`) package specifier (neither of which starts with `.` or `/`). Verified the existing BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT regex needed no change: its `(^|\/)src\/(?!utils(?:\/|$))` anchor already matches a leading-`/` string via the `\/` alternative (confirmed `/src/utils/format` stays exempt via the `utils` lookahead, and `/src/pages/Something`/`/src/api/x` are now flagged, matching the task's worked examples) -- the regex itself was never the bug, only the leading-character gate in front of it.
decisions.rationale: This is the precise, narrow fix pr-decision's verification called for: Vite's dev-server resolver genuinely resolves a root-absolute `/src/...` specifier against the project root (verified via server.pluginContainer.resolveId per the referenced task), so it's not a purely theoretical specifier shape, and main's pre-#417 rule did flag it -- #417's bare-package fix was too broad, excluding every non-dot-leading specifier including this one. Deliberately did NOT also treat a leading `~` as blocked (the original checklist wording floated `/`/`~`): nothing in this project's actual Vite/Playwright toolchain was verified to resolve a `~`-prefixed specifier against src/, unlike the `/`-rooted case, so flagging it would be speculative rather than evidence-based -- left as a documented non-goal in the extracted rule module's own comment rather than silently doing extra unverified work beyond what was asked.

decisions.decision: Extracted the rule and its BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT/isBlockedSrcSource/isTypeOnlyDeclaration helpers out of frontend/eslint.config.js into a new standalone ESM module, frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.js, imported by eslint.config.js. Kept it as plain JS with JSDoc types (not converted to TypeScript), added a persisted vitest test at frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.test.ts with two parts: (1) an it.each table test calling isBlockedSrcSource directly across every case this task's chain has found (bare/@scoped package allowed, root-absolute non-utils blocked, root-absolute utils allowed, relative blocked dirs, path-traversal blocked, relative utils/nested-utils/bare-utils-barrel allowed), and (2) an end-to-end 'wiring' test suite that imports eslint.config.js's actual default-exported flat config array, finds the tests/e2e/**/*.ts entry, asserts it registers the exact same rule object at 'error' severity, and then feeds that real config entry through ESLint's own Linter API (with typescript-eslint's parser, so import-type and other TS syntax parses) to confirm it still reports on a blocked static/dynamic import and stays silent on an allowed src/utils/ import, a type-only import, and the documented template-literal/variable dynamic-import residual gap.
decisions.rationale: Keeping the module plain JS (not .ts) avoids a real loading problem verified empirically: ESLint's flat-config loader only transpiles the *entry* config file on the fly when it's literally named eslint.config.ts (via an optional jiti/tsx peer dependency), not a module that entry file merely imports -- a sibling .ts file here would fail under Node's plain ESM loader when eslint.config.js imports it directly. The two-part test design directly answers the task's explicit 'wired in, not just correct' concern: a predicate-only table test would pass even if the rule were silently dropped from the plugins/rules wiring in eslint.config.js (e.g. a future refactor that renames the plugin key or forgets to re-import it), which is exactly the failure mode the Linter-based end-to-end half catches, since it exercises the real exported config object rather than a hand-rewritten copy. Chose this over eslint's RuleTester (considered and prototyped): RuleTester tests the rule object in isolation and would need its own from-scratch config/parser setup duplicating what eslint.config.js already defines, without ever touching the real exported array -- it couldn't have caught an 'unregistered from the real config' regression any better than the predicate table alone. The new eslint-rules/ directory is deliberately left out of both tsconfig.app.json's and tsconfig.node.json's include arrays (verified via `tsc --showConfig`): this exactly mirrors eslint.config.js's own pre-existing, unchanged treatment (it was never covered by either tsconfig project before this task either), so nothing regresses under `yarn tsc -b --noEmit`; the new test file still runs and is type-annotated for editor/author clarity, it's just not part of the tsc -b project graph, same as the config file importing it. Considered folding the test into tsconfig.app.json's include (which would make tsc -b check it) but rejected it as scope creep beyond this task's ask and a change to an unrelated file's behavior (every src/ test file would newly need to tolerate a tests/e2e/-style project boundary question) for marginal benefit, since vitest's own esbuild transform already catches any actual runtime/type-shape mismatch when the test runs.
